mechanism_narrative: The four-week accelerating decline in RETAIL_REC (-10.1 to -52.4) reflects entrenched reduction in non-essential outings; absent a policy reversal, this momentum persists and RETAIL_REC continues to fall over the next four weeks relative to the prior 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell every week from -10.1 to -52.4
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days despite the four-week monotonic decline, indicating momentum broke.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility signals tightening stay-at-home compliance; once RESIDENTIAL exceeds 20 points for two consecutive weeks, enforced restrictions suppress non-essential retail trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean exceeds 20 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 6.7 to 21.0 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises in the two weeks after RESIDENTIAL first exceeds 20 points, despite sustained high RESIDENTIAL readings.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous steep declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES jointly erode the commuting-linked habit of incidental retail stops; the combined drop produces a larger suppression of RETAIL_REC than either series predicts alone, persisting over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -20.6 to -55.4 while WORKPLACES fell from -16.0 to -40.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 28 days is no steeper than what TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone would predict via a simple additive model, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: Under an active lockdown regime where WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and RESIDENTIAL all show sustained movement toward closure/compliance extremes, enforced non-essential business restrictions keep RETAIL_REC suppressed in the immediate next week regardless of minor week-to-week fluctuations.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series moved toward lockdown extremes across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises week-over-week in the immediate next week while lockdown indicators (WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, RESIDENTIAL) remain at or beyond current extremes.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility falls below -15 points for two consecutive weeks, it signals a broader retreat from outdoor and discretionary activity beyond essential errands, which correlates with and precedes further reductions in RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls below -15 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was -15.6 in the latest week after swinging from +27.3 three weeks prior
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline, or rises, over the two weeks following two consecutive PARKS readings below -15 points.

mechanism_narrative: NSW autumn school holidays overlapping the Easter period (early-to-mid April 2020) combined with active lockdown measures lead families to avoid retail outings; as this holiday period concludes within the next week, no seasonal rebound occurs because lockdown dominates, so RETAIL_REC remains lower in the coming week.
evidence_refs: fact:decision point 2020-04-15 falls immediately after the Easter/school holiday window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a sharp rebound in the week immediately following the holiday period despite continued lockdown indicators, contradicting the seasonal-suppression claim.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM turning negative (-4.4) after three weeks of positive stockpiling-driven readings indicates consumers have exhausted pantry-loading behavior and are consolidating all errands, including retail; this joint shift in GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC trajectories signals compounding suppression of overall non-essential trips over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM dropped from 4.6 to -4.4 while RETAIL_REC fell from -36.6 to -52.4 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or improves over the next two weeks even as GROCERY_PHARM remains negative, indicating no compounding consolidation effect.

mechanism_narrative: As RETAIL_REC approaches a structural floor near -50 to -55 percent and week-over-week declines begin to decelerate, diminishing marginal suppression suggests mobility is nearing saturation; if the weekly rate of decline shrinks to under 5 points, RETAIL_REC is likely to stabilize or modestly rebound over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: week-over-week decline in RETAIL_REC narrows to less than 5 points
evidence_refs: fact:weekly RETAIL_REC changes were -21.9, -4.6, and -15.8 over the last three transitions, showing an uneven but bounded decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline by more than 5 points per week for two or more consecutive weeks after the deceleration trigger is observed.
